findings.title: Prompt and settings metadata keys and mode derivation are duplicated
findings.description: `describe_run_settings` in `core/models.py` builds the `system_prompt_mode`, `setting_sources` and `auto_memory` metadata keys for one-shot runs. The SDK-session branch in `dispatch.py` writes the same three keys again as string literals. It also re-derives the prompt mode with its own `PRESET_APPEND if session.seeded else PRESET` rule instead of going through `describe_system_prompt`. `ReviewResult.to_dict` adds a third copy of the two key names. The project rule is to define a comparison value once. Renaming a key now means editing several places, and the session path can drift from the one-shot path. Define the keys once, as constants or as a helper that accepts the session's values.

findings.title: Lines likely exceed the 88-character limit
findings.description:
Several new lines look longer than 88 characters:
- the `_read_turn` signature
- the `RateLimitRejected(...)` raise
- `_connect_lazy_session(run_id=effective_run_id, seed=resume_seed)` in `executor.py`
- the `PRESET_APPEND if config.instructions else PRESET` return in `models.py`
- the `system_prompt_mode` line in `review/models.py`

I could not confirm the configured `line-length`, so this may be a project-wide override. If the limit is 88, `ruff format` or `ruff check` will fail on these lines. Run the formatter and apply the result.

findings.title: Session code reads config files directly
findings.description: `SDKExecutionSession` and `open_pipeline_session` call `get_typed_config` themselves, so session logic now does config file I/O. The tests have to patch `get_typed_config` in the module to cope. Passing the timeout and settings policy in at construction would be more testable. This is minor, because the lookup runs only when a dispatch is already waiting.

findings.title: Test helpers are loosely typed
findings.description: `sdk_text`, `scripted_session` and `typed_config` return `object` or take bare `type`. As a result the tests need many `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments. This is not wrong, but strict pyright is meant to cover tests, and precise return types would remove most of the ignores. Also, `test_executor_each.py` imports `phase_artifact_cf_client` from the conftest. That helper is not in the diff, and I did not confirm it exists.

findings.title: Exception handling and failure observability
findings.description: The new broad catches comply with the project rules. `_stop_background` catches `Exception` with `# noqa: BLE001`, a justifying comment, and `logger.exception`. `_reconnect` logs with `logger.exception`, records `unusable_reason` and re-raises. Later calls then fail fast through `_require_usable`. The idle timeout, the stream ending with an agent still running, and the discarded follow-up turn each log at WARNING or raise. Tests cover each of these paths.

findings.title: Config and settings policy
findings.description: Bool coercion is lenient on case and whitespace and fails explicitly on bad input. `get_typed_config` handles `bool` before `int`. The settings policy sits in one module. `sdk_settings_options` copies `base_env` rather than mutating it. A parametrized per-path test asserts the policy for every automated SDK path.
